extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in bibliometrics, scientometrics, digital libraries, and information retrieval
extracted.subtask_description: Narrative review of empirical studies (2006–2018) about what citation counts measure, focusing on citation content/context analyses, citation motivation, technical/methodological developments, and features (context, semantics, location, polarity) relevant to interpreting citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation content and context analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies that perform citation content and context analyses to understand why and how citations are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review describes (new) studies on citation content and context analyses; technical developments (richer meta-data and machine-readable formats) have enabled citation context analyses of large datasets in comprehensive studies, which was not possible previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation motivation studies (surveys and interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that explores the citation motivation of scholars through surveys or interviews to uncover reasons for citing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These studies investigate scholars' motivations and reveal that a paper may be cited for very different scientific and non-scientific reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage technical developments (metadata and machine-readable formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of richer metadata and machine-readable paper formats to enable large-scale and automated citation analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper highlights recent technical developments (richer meta-data, machine-readable formats) that have resulted in citation context analyses of large datasets and facilitated computational approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of computational and machine learning techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of computational and machine learning methods to determine citation functions and polarities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many recent studies have used computational and machine learning techniques; some attempts aim to overcome methodological weaknesses of previous studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated recognition of citation functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated methods to recognize the function (role/purpose) of citations within texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The automated recognition of citation functions seems to have the potential to greatly enhance citation indices and information retrieval capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of diverse scientific and non-scientific citation reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness that citations can reflect a variety of scientific and non-scientific reasons rather than a single dimension of 'impact'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review's empirical studies demonstrate that a paper may be cited for very different scientific and non-scientific reasons; this finding accords with Bornmann and Daniel (2008).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze citation context
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the local textual context around a citation to infer meaning, function, and the reason for citing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review emphasizes citation context as a primary feature to analyze when seeking to understand the relationship between citing and cited documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze semantics and linguistic patterns in citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the semantics and linguistic patterns of citation sentences and surrounding text to characterize citation function and sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantics and linguistic patterns in citations are listed as primary features that should be analyzed to better understand citing–cited relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze citation locations within citing documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider where within the citing document a citation appears (e.g., introduction, methods, discussion) as an indicator of its role and importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation locations within the citing document are highlighted as a primary feature to analyze for understanding why a work was cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze citation polarity (negative, neutral, positive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the sentiment or polarity of a citation—whether it is negative, neutral, or positive—as part of citation-content analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation polarity (negative, neutral, positive) is identified as a primary analytic feature; machine-learning methods have been used to determine polarities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address methodological weaknesses in citation studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly identify and attempt to overcome methodological weaknesses present in prior citation research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review notes that some recent computational studies have attempted to overcome methodological weaknesses of previous studies, implying methodological rigor and validation are important criteria.
